# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 24 (Bu-Vb Pc24)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc24
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 24
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** 24. Accusing monks of teaching nuns for profit
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-bu-vb-pc24
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Āmisa-sikkhāpada* is the twenty-fourth rule in the *Pācittiya* section of the Pali *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* (*Vinaya Piṭaka*), belonging to the *Ovādavagga* (the chapter concerning the exhortation of nuns) [Catalog; SuttaCentral]. The rule stipulates that if a monk accuses other monks of instructing the nuns merely for the sake of worldly gain (*āmisa*) or material benefit, intending to discredit them, he incurs an offense requiring confession (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral; Sujato 2009]. Bhikkhu Sujato notes in his study of the nuns' discipline that while monks themselves are enjoined not to give instruction out of a desire for worldly advantages such as receiving homage, falsely accusing another monk of teaching for material benefits constitutes an offense under this rule [Sujato 2009].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral demonstrate that this precept is shared across all major extant Vinaya traditions [SuttaCentral]. It appears as rule 24 in the *Pātimokkhas* and *Vibhaṅgas* of the Theravāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṃghika, Lokottaravāda, and Kāśyapīya traditions, and as rule 23 in the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, and Dharmaguptaka recensions (extant in Sanskrit, Classical Chinese, and Tibetan), as well as rule 25 in Chinese translations related to the *Upāliparipṛcchā* [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis via DharmaNexus shows extensive internal text reuse across 87 Pali texts, particularly with adjacent and related *Vibhaṅga* rulings including *Pācittiya* 13, 21, 2, and 23, and with post-canonical Vinaya literature such as the *Vinayavinicchaya-ṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also confirms cross-linguistic alignment with the Tibetan *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003-3), corresponding to the Mūlasarvāstivāda transmission identified by SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
